original_question: Given a group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its centerpole numbers c_r^λ(G).
target_in_paper: Problem 11.3, which specializes the general centerpole-number problem of §10 to groups endowed with the asymptotic-dimension measure and the family of central symmetries, asking for the centerpole numbers c_r^λ(G). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct topic (centerpole numbers of groups), the correct ambient viewpoint (a group G treated as a symmetry measure space with the asymptotic-dimension measure), and the correct symmetry type (central symmetries). This is very close to the official open problem stated in §11. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
missing_details: The paper’s official target is the open problem for an arbitrary group G, not only for Abelian groups; the text immediately after Problem 11.3 says that only some information is available for Abelian groups and that much less is known for non-commutative groups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
The family S of symmetries is not defined explicitly in the draft: these are the central symmetries s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c, indexed by c∈G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The draft does not define c_r^λ(G): it is the least cardinality of a set C⊂G (equivalently, of the corresponding subfamily of central symmetries) such that every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic subset A with asdim(A)≥λ and A=cA^{-1}c for some c∈C; if no such C exists, the value is ∞. This comes from the general definition in §10 specialized to the group setting of §11. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
The quantifiers are implicit: r is a cardinal counting colors, and λ is the threshold in the value set of the asymptotic-dimension measure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
The symmetry condition on the sought monochromatic subset should be stated explicitly as A=cA^{-1}c for some center c in the chosen set C. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The draft does not say what kind of colorings are meant. In §11 the measure is assigned to all subsets of G, so the natural formulation is for arbitrary r-colorings χ:G→r, not a separate Borel-coloring version. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

The draft mentions asdim but does not explain that λ measures the required asymptotic dimension of the monochromatic symmetric subset; the paper’s notation allows many λ-levels, so this should be made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
For maximum faithfulness to the paper, the verb should be 'calculate or evaluate' rather than only 'calculate or estimate.' ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
refined_question: Given an arbitrary group G, regarded as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) where S={s_c:c∈G} and s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c, calculate or evaluate, for each cardinal r and each asymptotic-dimension threshold λ, the centerpole number c_r^λ(G): the least cardinality of a set C⊂G such that every r-coloring χ:G→r contains a monochromatic subset A⊂G with asdim(A)≥λ and A=cA^{-1}c for some c∈C, with c_r^λ(G)=∞ if no such C exists. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening because §11 explicitly passes from the general definition of centerpole numbers in §10 to the special case of groups endowed with the asymptotic-dimension measure and central symmetries, and then states the official open problem as Problem 11.3. Your draft already mirrors that specialization almost verbatim; the refinement only restores the hidden definition of c_r^λ(G), the quantifiers on r and λ, and the symmetry condition A=cA^{-1}c. The nearby remark that only partial Abelian information is known, while non-commutative cases remain much less understood, confirms that the intended scope is all groups and not a narrower neighboring problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))
